Fungal infection.overview: A fungal infection occurs when fungi overcome the body's defenses and infect tissue, commonly affecting the skin, nails, or mucosal surfaces (athlete's foot, ringworm, candidiasis).

prescription.name: Clotrimazole / Terbinafine 1% Cream
prescription.instruction: Apply thin layer twice daily to cleaned, dried affected areas

prescription.name: Fluconazole 150mg (Oral)
prescription.instruction: Single weekly dose if prescribed for extensive cutaneous infection

prescription.name: Antifungal Dusting Powder
prescription.instruction: Dust inside shoes and skin folds daily to keep dry

care: Keep skin clean, thoroughly dried, and exposed to air when possible.
Wear loose-fitting, breathable cotton clothing and change daily.
Avoid sharing towels, bed linens, or personal grooming items.
diet: Reduce refined sugar intake, which may promote yeast proliferation.
Incorporate probiotic-rich foods like plain yogurt and fermented kefir.
Stay hydrated with 2.5L water daily to bolster skin barrier recovery.

Allergy.overview: An exaggerated immune response to harmless environmental allergens (pollen, dust mites, pet dander), causing mucosal inflammation, sneezing, and ocular irritation.

prescription.name: Cetirizine 10mg / Levocetirizine 5mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet once daily at bedtime

prescription.name: Fluticasone Propionate Nasal Spray
prescription.instruction: 1-2 sprays per nostril once daily morning

prescription.name: Saline Nasal Irrigation
prescription.instruction: Rinse nasal cavities twice daily with isotonic saline

care: Keep windows closed during high pollen or windy conditions.
Use HEPA air filtration in living and sleeping quarters.
Wash bedding weekly in hot water (>130°F / 55°C).
diet: Consume foods rich in quercetin (apples, red onions, berries).
Incorporate anti-inflammatory omega-3 fatty acids (flaxseeds, walnuts).
Avoid known trigger foods or excessive histaminic foods during flare-ups.

GERD.overview: A digestive disorder where stomach acid persistently flows back into the esophagus, irritating the lining and causing heartburn, regurgitation, and chest discomfort.

prescription.name: Pantoprazole 40mg / Omeprazole 20mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet 30 minutes before breakfast on an empty stomach

prescription.name: Antacid Suspension (Magaldrate + Simethicone)
prescription.instruction: 10-15 ml after meals and before bedtime as needed

prescription.name: Famotidine 20mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet before dinner for nocturnal symptoms

care: Elevate the head of your bed by 6-8 inches (15-20 cm).
Wait at least 3 hours after eating before lying down or going to sleep.
Eat smaller, more frequent meals rather than large heavy dinners.
diet: Avoid acidic citrus, tomatoes, caffeine, chocolate, and carbonated beverages.
Minimize deep-fried, fatty, spicy foods and mint.
Incorporate oatmeal, non-citrus fruits (bananas, melons), and lean poultry.

Chronic cholestasis.overview: A reduction or stagnation of bile flow from the liver to the duodenum, leading to bile acid accumulation, jaundice, and intense pruritus.

prescription.name: Ursodeoxycholic Acid (UDCA) 300mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet 2-3 times daily with meals under specialist guidance

prescription.name: Cholestyramine 4g
prescription.instruction: Mix with water/juice taken 1 hour after breakfast for itching

prescription.name: Fat-Soluble Vitamin Supplement (A, D, E, K)
prescription.instruction: Daily formulation to counteract biliary malabsorption

care: Regular hepatic liver panel monitoring (ALT, AST, Bilirubin, Alk Phos).
Avoid all alcohol consumption and hepatotoxic medications.
Maintain cool baths and gentle moisturizers for bile salt skin irritation.
diet: Adopt a low-fat, nutrient-dense Mediterranean diet.
Incorporate medium-chain triglyceride (MCT) fats for easier absorption.
Stay well-hydrated to assist renal clearance of circulating bile acids.

Drug Reaction.overview: An immunological or non-immunological adverse cutaneous reaction to an ingested or administered pharmaceutical agent, producing rashes or urticaria.

prescription.name: IMMEDIATE DISCONTINUATION of Suspected Drug
prescription.instruction: Stop offending drug immediately under physician supervision

prescription.name: Fexofenadine 180mg / Bilastine 20mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet once daily morning for histamine relief

prescription.name: Hydrocortisone 1% Topical Cream / Calamine
prescription.instruction: Apply gently to itchy patches 2 times daily

care: Document the offending medication and carry an allergy alert card.
Seek immediate emergency care if facial swelling, lips or breathing are involved.
Avoid hot showers and harsh soaps that exacerbate skin inflammation.
diet: Drink plentiful cool fluids and electrolytes.
Eat soothing, non-spicy foods to prevent secondary mucosal irritation.
Avoid artificial dyes and preservatives during the recovery phase.

Peptic ulcer disease.overview: Sores that develop on the inside lining of the stomach or duodenum, usually caused by H. pylori infection or long-term NSAID painkiller use.

prescription.name: Esomeprazole 40mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet once daily 30 minutes before breakfast

prescription.name: Sucralfate 1g Suspension
prescription.instruction: 10ml 4 times daily, 1 hour before meals and at bedtime

prescription.name: H. Pylori Eradication Regimen (if positive)
prescription.instruction: Triple/quadruple antibiotic therapy under physician direction

care: Completely avoid NSAID painkillers like ibuprofen, naproxen, and aspirin.
Stop smoking and eliminate alcoholic beverages which erode mucosal barriers.
Do not skip meals; keep regular consistent eating schedules.
diet: Eat fiber-rich foods, particularly soluble fiber (oats, legumes, vegetables).
Include probiotic foods (plain yogurt, kefir) to inhibit pathogenic bacteria.
Avoid highly spiced chili peppers, black pepper, and excessive coffee.

AIDS.overview: Advanced retroviral immunocompromise caused by Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), resulting in depletion of CD4+ T lymphocytes.

prescription.name: Antiretroviral Therapy (ART)
prescription.instruction: Combination antiretroviral regimen prescribed by infectious disease specialist

prescription.name: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim DS)
prescription.instruction: 1 tablet daily for opportunistic infection prophylaxis

prescription.name: Multivitamin with Zinc and Selenium
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet daily with food

care: Strict adherence to ART timing without missing doses.
Regular CD4 cell counts and HIV viral load monitoring every 3-6 months.
Practice stringent food hygiene to avoid waterborne and foodborne pathogens.
diet: High-calorie, high-protein diet (eggs, legumes, fish, nuts) to prevent wasting.
Only consume thoroughly cooked foods and clean boiled/filtered water.
Eat frequent small nutrient-dense meals throughout the day.

Diabetes.overview: A chronic metabolic condition characterized by insulin resistance and relative insulin deficiency, leading to persistently elevated blood glucose.

prescription.name: Metformin 500mg (Doctor Prescribed)
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet with or after evening meal

prescription.name: Capillary Blood Glucose Log
prescription.instruction: Test fasting and 2-hour postprandial glucose 3 times a week

prescription.name: HbA1c Glycated Hemoglobin Test
prescription.instruction: Comprehensive laboratory assessment every 3 months

care: Engage in 30 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise (brisk walking) 5 days/week.
Perform daily foot examinations to identify any blisters, cuts, or sores early.
Maintain strict blood pressure and lipid panel control.
diet: Eliminate refined sugars, sugary beverages, pastries, and white flour.
Base meals on low-glycemic complex carbohydrates (quinoa, barley, vegetables).
Incorporate lean proteins and healthy fats to blunt post-meal glucose spikes.

Gastroenteritis.overview: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines typically caused by viral or bacterial infection, resulting in diarrhea, vomiting, and cramps.

prescription.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)
prescription.instruction: Dissolve 1 packet in 1 liter clean water; sip 200ml after each loose stool

prescription.name: Ondansetron 4mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet 15 minutes before oral intake if nausea prevents hydration

prescription.name: Probiotic S. boulardii 250mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 capsule twice daily with lukewarm water

care: Prioritize active electrolyte replenishment to avoid dehydration.
Rest comfortably and avoid intense physical exertion.
Monitor urine output (should remain pale yellow, not dark or absent).
diet: Follow BRAT diet during acute recovery: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast.
Drink clear broths, diluted coconut water, and herbal chamomile tea.
Avoid dairy products, greasy foods, caffeine, and alcohol for 5-7 days.

Bronchial Asthma.overview: A chronic inflammatory disorder of the airways causing episodic airway constriction, hyperresponsiveness, wheezing, and breathlessness.

prescription.name: Salbutamol / Albuterol Inhaler (100mcg)
prescription.instruction: Inhale 1-2 puffs with spacer as needed for acute shortness of breath

prescription.name: Budesonide 200mcg / Formoterol Inhaler
prescription.instruction: Inhale 1 puff twice daily; rinse mouth thoroughly with water afterward

prescription.name: Peak Expiratory Flow Meter
prescription.instruction: Record morning and evening PEF readings to monitor airway control

care: Always carry your rescue bronchodilator inhaler wherever you go.
Identify and eliminate environmental asthma triggers (smoke, cold air, pet dander).
Establish an Asthma Action Plan with your pulmonologist.
diet: Eat antioxidant-rich colorful vegetables and fruits (vitamin C and E).
Avoid foods containing sulfites or artificial preservatives (dried fruits, wine).
Maintain a healthy body weight to reduce respiratory workload.

Hypertension.overview: A long-term medical condition in which systemic arterial blood pressure is persistently elevated (>130/80 mmHg), increasing cardiovascular risk.

prescription.name: Amlodipine 5mg / Telmisartan 40mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet once daily morning under physician prescription

prescription.name: Digital Home Blood Pressure Monitor
prescription.instruction: Record morning and evening readings twice weekly seated quietly

prescription.name: Routine Serum Electrolytes & Renal Panel
prescription.instruction: Monitor creatinine and potassium every 6 months

care: Strictly limit dietary sodium intake to under 1,500 - 2,000 mg per day.
Engage in 150 minutes of moderate aerobic cardiovascular exercise weekly.
Practice stress reduction techniques (mindfulness, diaphragmatic breathing).
diet: Adhere to the DASH Diet (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension).
Increase potassium-rich whole foods (bananas, sweet potatoes, spinach).
Minimize processed foods, canned soups, cured meats, and alcohol.

Migraine.overview: A neurological disorder characterized by recurrent, severe throbbing unilateral headaches often accompanied by nausea, photophobia, and sensory aura.

prescription.name: Sumatriptan 50mg / Zolmitriptan 2.5mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet at the earliest onset of migraine attack (max 2/day)

prescription.name: Naproxen Sodium 500mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet with food for moderate headache pain

prescription.name: Propranolol / Topiramate (Preventive)
prescription.instruction: Daily prescription if attacks occur >4 days per month

care: Rest in a quiet, dark, cool room with a cold compress across forehead.
Maintain consistent sleep schedules; avoid sleep deprivation or oversleeping.
Keep a headache diary to pinpoint individual dietary and sensory triggers.
diet: Stay steadily hydrated throughout the day; dehydration triggers attacks.
Limit aged cheeses, red wine, chocolate, cured meats containing nitrates, and MSG.
Ensure regular meal timing to prevent hypoglycemia-induced migraines.

Cervical spondylosis.overview: Age-related wear and tear affecting cervical spinal disks and vertebrae, causing neck stiffness, local pain, and occasional radicular numbness.

prescription.name: Paracetamol 650mg / Ibuprofen 400mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet with meals twice daily for acute neck discomfort

prescription.name: Thiocolchicoside / Baclofen 10mg
prescription.instruction: Muscle relaxant taken at bedtime for acute neck spasm

prescription.name: Topical Diclofenac 1.16% Gel
prescription.instruction: Gently massage onto posterior cervical region 3 times daily

care: Perform gentle cervical isometric and range-of-motion physical therapy exercises.
Use an ergonomic contoured cervical pillow to maintain neutral spinal alignment.
Avoid prolonged forward-head posture when viewing computer screens or mobile phones.
diet: Ensure adequate dietary calcium (1,000-1,200 mg/day) and Vitamin D3 (1,000 IU/day).
Eat anti-inflammatory foods (fatty fish, olive oil, turmeric, leafy greens).
Maintain optimal hydration to nourish intervertebral disk hydration.

Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).overview: A critical emergency resulting from rupture of a cerebral blood vessel, causing localized brain tissue compression and sudden motor/sensory paralysis.

prescription.name: IMMEDIATE EMERGENCY AMBULANCE TRANSPORT (911 / 108)
prescription.instruction: Immediate transfer to a certified Comprehensive Stroke Center

prescription.name: Strict Hospital Neurosurgical Management
prescription.instruction: Blood pressure regulation, neurocritical monitoring, surgical decompression if indicated

prescription.name: Multidisciplinary Neuro-Rehabilitation
prescription.instruction: Physical, occupational, and speech-language therapy initiated upon stabilization

care: Call emergency services immediately. Note the exact time symptoms started.
Do NOT give the patient any food, drink, or oral medications (choking risk).
Keep patient lying down on their side with head slightly elevated if vomiting.
diet: Strict medically supervised clinical enteral or pureed nutrition in hospital.
Lifelong low-sodium, cardiovascular-protective Mediterranean diet after stabilization.
Complete cessation of tobacco and alcohol.

Jaundice.overview: Yellowish discoloration of the skin, sclera, and mucous membranes caused by elevated bilirubin levels from hepatic dysfunction, hemolysis, or biliary obstruction.

prescription.name: Silymarin / Milk Thistle Extract 140mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 capsule twice daily with meals as hepatic support

prescription.name: Comprehensive Liver Function Test (LFT)
prescription.instruction: Measure total/direct bilirubin, AST, ALT, ALP and viral hepatitis markers

prescription.name: Vitamin B-Complex & Vitamin C
prescription.instruction: Daily therapeutic formulation to support cellular hepatocyte repair

care: Strictly refrain from all alcohol and hepatotoxic substances (e.g. high-dose acetaminophen).
Get plenty of bed rest to optimize hepatic blood circulation.
Seek immediate hospital attention if accompanied by confusion, lethargy, or dark stools.
diet: Consume light, easily digestible carbohydrate-rich foods (porridge, boiled rice, papayas).
Drink fresh sugarcane juice, coconut water, and clean boiled water throughout the day.
Strictly avoid deep-fried, oily, fatty meats, and spicy dishes.

Malaria.overview: A life-threatening parasitic infection transmitted through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes, characterized by paroxysms of shaking chills and high fever.

prescription.name: Artemether-Lumefantrine (ACT)
prescription.instruction: Standard 6-dose course over 3 days taken with fatty food/milk as prescribed

prescription.name: Paracetamol 650mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet every 6 hours for body temperature >101°F (38.3°C)

prescription.name: Oral Electrolytes & Hydration
prescription.instruction: Drink 3 liters of fluids daily to protect renal perfusion

care: Complete the full course of antimalarial medications even if feeling better.
Sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets and use mosquito repellents.
Monitor serial blood smears or rapid diagnostic tests to verify parasitemia clearance.
diet: High-calorie, easily digestible liquid and semi-solid diet during febrile stages.
Electrolyte-rich coconut water, fresh orange juice, and vegetable soups.
Gradually reintroduce high-protein foods (lentils, steamed poultry) as appetite recovers.

Chicken pox.overview: A highly contagious viral infection caused by the Varicella-Zoster virus, resulting in an itchy vesicular blister rash, fever, and malaise.

prescription.name: Calamine Lotion
prescription.instruction: Apply gently to itchy lesions 3-4 times daily to soothe skin

prescription.name: Cetirizine 10mg / Diphenhydramine
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet at bedtime to reduce nighttime scratching

prescription.name: Paracetamol 500mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet for fever (NEVER give aspirin to children/teens - Reye syndrome risk)

care: Keep patient isolated until all blisters have fully dried into crusty scabs.
Keep fingernails trimmed short and clean to prevent secondary bacterial skin infections.
Bathe in lukewarm oatmeal baths to alleviate generalized itchiness.
diet: Soft, cool, bland foods if mouth lesions are present (smoothies, ice pops, yogurt).
Generous fluid intake (cool water, diluted fruit juices, broths).
Avoid salty, highly acidic, or hard crunchy foods that irritate oral sores.

Dengue.overview: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing high fever, severe retro-orbital pain, muscle/joint aches, and potential thrombocytopenia (low platelet count).

prescription.name: Paracetamol 650mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet every 6 hours for fever (STRICTLY AVOID Aspirin/Ibuprofen - bleeding risk)

prescription.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) Therapy
prescription.instruction: Drink 2.5 - 3.5 liters of oral fluids daily to prevent capillary leak shock

prescription.name: Daily Complete Blood Count (CBC)
prescription.instruction: Track platelet count and hematocrit daily until fever defervescence

care: Absolute physical bed rest during both febrile and critical defervescence phases.
Watch closely for warning signs: severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, mucosal bleeding.
Use mosquito nets and repellents to prevent transmitting virus to household members.
diet: Drink fluids constantly: ORS, tender coconut water, pomegranate juice, barley water.
Papaya leaf extract syrup can be consumed as supportive therapy.
Eat light, soft, nutrient-rich meals (khichdi, vegetable purees).

Typhoid.overview: A systemic bacterial infection caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi, contracted via contaminated food or water, causing sustained step-ladder fever and abdominal distress.

prescription.name: Cefixime 200mg / Azithromycin 500mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet twice daily with food as prescribed by physician

prescription.name: Paracetamol 650mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet for temperatures >101°F up to 4 times daily

prescription.name: Probiotics & Digestive Enzymes
prescription.instruction: Take daily to assist intestinal flora restoration post-antibiotics

care: Complete entire antibiotic regimen without interruption to avoid chronic carrier state.
Drink only boiled or certified bottled water and wash hands rigorously before meals.
Rest extensively and monitor for complications such as intestinal bleeding.
diet: High-calorie, low-fiber, bland soft diet (custards, boiled potatoes, rice gruel).
Avoid raw vegetables, unpeeled fruits, coarse grains, and fried spicy foods.
Ensure abundant clean fluid intake (boiled water, clear soups, electrolytes).

hepatitis A.overview: An acute, usually self-limiting liver infection caused by the Hepatitis A virus, transmitted predominantly through the fecal-oral route via contaminated water or food.

prescription.name: Supportive Care & Symptom Relief
prescription.instruction: Rest, antiemetics if nauseated, no specific antiviral required

prescription.name: B-Complex with Vitamin C
prescription.instruction: Daily tablet to support hepatic metabolic recovery

prescription.name: Liver Panel Monitoring
prescription.instruction: Repeat liver enzymes and bilirubin weekly until normal

care: Strict avoidance of alcohol and all non-essential medications.
Thorough handwashing with soap after using the restroom and before food preparation.
Adequate physical rest during the acute jaundice phase.
diet: Nutrient-rich, easily digestible high-carbohydrate meals.
Fresh fruits, fruit juices, sugarcane juice, and boiled vegetables.
Avoid fatty foods, heavy oils, fried meats, and artificial seasonings.

Hepatitis B.overview: A serious liver infection caused by the Hepatitis B virus, transmitted through blood, sexual fluids, or perinatal contact, capable of chronic progression.

prescription.name: Tenofovir / Entecavir (Specialist Prescribed)
prescription.instruction: Antiviral therapy if chronic active disease with elevated viral load

prescription.name: HBsAg, HBeAg, and HBV DNA Viral Load
prescription.instruction: Laboratory monitoring every 3-6 months by gastroenterologist

prescription.name: Abdominal Ultrasound & AFP Screening
prescription.instruction: Annual hepatic surveillance for hepatocellular health

care: Family members and intimate partners should receive the Hepatitis B vaccine series.
Absolute prohibition of alcohol consumption to prevent accelerated fibrosis.
Never share razors, toothbrushes, needles, or personal manicure items.
diet: Balanced, liver-supportive diet with high antioxidant content (berries, greens).
Moderate lean protein intake (legumes, fish, tofu, eggs).
Limit sodium and heavily processed foods.

Hepatitis C.overview: A bloodborne viral infection that causes inflammation of the liver, curable in >95% of cases with modern direct-acting antiviral (DAA) medications.

prescription.name: Sofosbuvir + Velpatasvir (DAA Regimen)
prescription.instruction: 1 tablet once daily with food as prescribed by hepatologist

prescription.name: HCV RNA Quantitative PCR Test
prescription.instruction: Verify sustained virologic response (SVR12) 12 weeks after treatment

prescription.name: Liver Fibrosis Assessment (FibroScan)
prescription.instruction: Assess degree of baseline liver scarring prior to therapy

care: Complete all 12 weeks of DAA pills without missing doses for full viral cure.
Completely abstain from alcohol consumption.
Practice safe blood precautions; do not donate blood, organs, or semen.
diet: Plant-forward Mediterranean diet rich in whole vegetables and grains.
Moderate coffee consumption (2-3 cups/day) has documented liver-protective associations.
Avoid raw or undercooked shellfish (Vibrio vulnerability in liver disease).

Hepatitis D.overview: A subviral satellite that can only propagate in individuals with active Hepatitis B virus infection, resulting in accelerated liver disease.

prescription.name: Pegylated Interferon Alfa-2a / Bulevirtide
prescription.instruction: Specialist hepatology therapeutic regimen under hospital monitoring

prescription.name: HDV RNA & Quantitative HBsAg Testing
prescription.instruction: Periodic virological monitoring to assess treatment efficacy

prescription.name: Hepatoprotective Antioxidant Support
prescription.instruction: Daily formulation supporting cellular resilience

care: Strict adherence to hepatology appointments and blood surveillance.
Zero tolerance for alcohol or unprescribed over-the-counter supplements.
Screen for portal hypertension and esophageal varices.
diet: Strict sodium restriction (<2,000 mg/day) if portal pressure is elevated.
Nutrient-dense, low-fat, high-fiber meals.
Ensure balanced caloric intake to prevent muscle wasting.

Hepatitis E.overview: An acute waterborne viral hepatitis infection transmitted via fecal-oral contamination, generally self-limiting but severe in pregnant individuals.

prescription.name: Supportive Outpatient Care & Rest
prescription.instruction: Rest and hydration; infection typically resolves spontaneously within 4-6 weeks

prescription.name: Liver Function Monitoring
prescription.instruction: Bi-weekly blood tests to ensure transaminases are resolving toward normal

prescription.name: Electrolyte & Hydration Support
prescription.instruction: Maintain oral fluids and clean water intake

care: Special vigilance and immediate hospital admission if patient is pregnant.
Only consume thoroughly boiled or treated drinking water.
Practice rigorous hand sanitization before preparing food.
diet: Light, easily digestible carbohydrate-rich foods (congee, fruit compotes).
Fresh coconut water, buttermilk, herbal teas, and clean broths.
Zero fatty, fried, or spicy meals.

Alcoholic hepatitis.overview: Acute liver inflammation caused by heavy, prolonged alcohol consumption, leading to hepatocellular damage, jaundice, and potential liver failure.

prescription.name: ABSOLUTE AND PERMANENT ALCOHOL CESSATION
prescription.instruction: Immediate and complete cessation of all alcohol is essential for survival

prescription.name: Prednisolone 40mg (if Maddrey DF >= 32)
prescription.instruction: Corticosteroid therapy prescribed in-hospital for severe presentation

prescription.name: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) 100mg + Folate
prescription.instruction: Take daily to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy and neurological injury

care: Engage with addiction medicine specialist and support groups (AA).
Seek immediate emergency care if abdominal swelling (ascites) or confusion occurs.
Frequent monitoring of coagulation (INR) and bilirubin.
diet: High-protein, high-calorie nutritional therapy to overcome malnutrition.
Sodium restriction (<2g/day) to prevent fluid accumulation in abdomen and legs.
Eat frequent small meals including a late-evening carbohydrate snack.

Tuberculosis.overview: A serious airborne bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, primarily attacking the lungs and causing chronic cough, hemoptysis, and night sweats.

prescription.name: Directly Observed Therapy (DOTS) Regimen
prescription.instruction: Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol (RIPE) daily as prescribed

prescription.name: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) 25-50mg
prescription.instruction: Take daily to prevent isoniazid-induced peripheral neuropathy

prescription.name: Sputum Smear & Culture Monitoring
prescription.instruction: Perform periodic monthly sputum evaluations to confirm conversion

care: Never skip a single dose of TB medications to prevent multi-drug resistance (MDR-TB).
Wear a well-fitted mask and ensure cross-ventilation in living spaces until non-infectious.
Household contacts must be screened for latent TB infection.
diet: High-protein, calorie-dense diet (eggs, milk, legumes, nuts) to regain lost body weight.
Foods rich in vitamins A, C, E, and Zinc to bolster cell-mediated immunity.
Avoid all alcohol and tobacco products.

Common Cold.overview: A mild, self-limiting viral infection of the upper respiratory tract (rhinovirus, coronavirus), causing nasal congestion, sneezing, sore throat, and low-grade malaise.

prescription.name: Paracetamol 500mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet every 6-8 hours as needed for body ache and fever

prescription.name: Saline Nasal Drops / Spray
prescription.instruction: 2-3 drops in each nostril 3-4 times daily to relieve congestion

prescription.name: Steam Inhalation with Menthol / Eucalyptus
prescription.instruction: Inhale warm steam 2 times daily for 10 minutes

care: Get 8 hours of restorative sleep to empower immune response.
Wash hands frequently and use tissues to prevent spreading virus to others.
Gargle with warm salt water (1/2 tsp salt in 1 cup warm water) for sore throat.
diet: Drink plentiful warm fluids: ginger-lemon tea, chicken broth, herbal teas.
Consume foods rich in Vitamin C (oranges, guavas, amla, bell peppers).
Honey with warm water or ginger juice to soothe cough reflex.

Pneumonia.overview: An infection that inflames the air sacs (alveoli) in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or purulent sputum, causing productive cough, fever, and pleuritic pain.

prescription.name: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 625mg / Azithromycin 500mg
prescription.instruction: Take twice daily with meals as prescribed by physician

prescription.name: Paracetamol 650mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet every 6 hours for high temperature and pleuritic chest ache

prescription.name: N-Acetylcysteine 600mg
prescription.instruction: Effervescent tablet in water once daily morning to thin mucous secretions

care: Use an incentive spirometer or perform deep breathing exercises hourly.
Monitor oxygen saturation (SpO2) with a pulse oximeter; seek ER if <93%.
Strict bed rest and complete the full prescribed course of antibiotics.
diet: Drink at least 2.5 to 3 liters of fluids daily to liquefy bronchial secretions.
Warm soups, broths, and high-protein meals to preserve respiratory muscle strength.
Avoid cold refrigerated drinks and dairy if it thickens phlegm sensation.

Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).overview: Swollen, inflamed veins in the lower rectum and anus, causing rectal bleeding during bowel movements, localized itching, and discomfort.

prescription.name: Topical Anesthetic & Anti-inflammatory Ointment (Hydrocortisone + Lidocaine)
prescription.instruction: Apply gently to affected rectal area after bowel movement and at bedtime

prescription.name: Psyllium Husk / Isabgol (Soluble Fiber)
prescription.instruction: 1-2 tablespoons in a full glass of water at bedtime to soften stool

prescription.name: Warm Sitz Bath
prescription.instruction: Soak anal area in warm water for 15-20 minutes, 2-3 times daily

care: Do not strain or sit on the toilet for prolonged periods (>5 minutes).
Use soft moist wipes or a bidet rather than dry rough toilet paper.
Stay physically active (daily walking) to stimulate natural bowel motility.
diet: High-fiber diet (25-35g/day): whole oats, beans, bran cereals, figs, prunes.
Drink a minimum of 2.5 - 3.0 liters of water daily so fiber can soften stools.
Avoid hot chili peppers, excessive alcohol, and heavy red meats.

Heart attack.overview: A life-threatening medical emergency where blood flow to a section of the heart muscle becomes abruptly blocked, starving myocardial tissue of oxygen.

prescription.name: CALL EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES (911 / 108) IMMEDIATELY
prescription.instruction: Request urgent cardiac ambulance dispatch with ECG equipment

prescription.name: Chewable Aspirin 300mg
prescription.instruction: Chew and swallow immediately if directed by emergency dispatch clinician

prescription.name: Sublingual Nitroglycerin 0.4mg
prescription.instruction: Place under tongue if previously prescribed and blood pressure is not low

care: Stop all activity immediately; sit or lie down comfortably in semi-upright posture.
Loosen tight clothing around neck and chest; stay calm and wait for ambulance.
Do NOT attempt to drive yourself to the hospital.
diet: Nil by mouth during acute emergency.
Long-term post-infarction: strict low-sodium, heart-healthy Mediterranean diet.
Permanently eliminate trans fats, fried foods, and tobacco smoke.

Varicose veins.overview: Enlarged, twisted, swollen superficial veins caused by weakened or damaged venous valves, typically in the lower extremities, leading to heaviness and aching.

prescription.name: Graduated Compression Stockings (Class II, 20-30 mmHg)
prescription.instruction: Put on in morning before getting out of bed; wear during daytime hours

prescription.name: Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction (MPFF) 500mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet twice daily with meals to improve venous tone

prescription.name: Topical Heparinoid / Horse Chestnut Gel
prescription.instruction: Apply upward strokes from ankle to calf 2 times daily

care: Elevate legs above the level of your heart for 15-20 minutes 3 times daily.
Avoid prolonged uninterrupted standing or sitting; flex calves and walk periodically.
Maintain a healthy body weight to diminish excessive venous hydrostatic pressure.
diet: Eat foods rich in flavonoids (blueberries, dark leafy greens, citrus bioflavonoids).
High-fiber diet to avoid chronic constipation and elevated intra-abdominal pressure.
Limit sodium intake to minimize dependent lower-extremity fluid retention.

Hypothyroidism.overview: An underactive thyroid gland that fails to produce adequate thyroid hormones (T3, T4), resulting in sluggish metabolism, weight gain, fatigue, and cold intolerance.

prescription.name: Levothyroxine Sodium (25-100 mcg as prescribed)
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet once daily morning on an empty stomach with water, 30-60 min before breakfast

prescription.name: Serum TSH & Free T4 Monitoring
prescription.instruction: Repeat blood test 6-8 weeks after starting or adjusting dosage, then annually

prescription.name: Separate Calcium / Iron Supplements
prescription.instruction: Take any calcium, iron, or antacid pills at least 4 hours apart from thyroid dose

care: Strict adherence to morning empty-stomach administration routine.
Keep regular sleep and physical activity schedules to boost metabolic rate.
Report any palpitations, tremors, or insomnia to doctor (signs of excess dose).
diet: Ensure adequate dietary iodine through iodized table salt and seafood.
Incorporate selenium-rich foods (Brazil nuts, sunflower seeds, fish).
Cook goitrogenic cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cabbage) thoroughly before eating.

Hyperthyroidism.overview: An overactive thyroid gland producing excessive quantities of thyroid hormone, driving an accelerated metabolic state with tremors, palpitations, weight loss, and heat intolerance.

prescription.name: Methimazole 5-20mg / Propylthiouracil (PTU)
prescription.instruction: Antithyroid medication taken daily exactly as directed by endocrinologist

prescription.name: Propranolol 20-40mg
prescription.instruction: Take 2-3 times daily to control tachycardia, tremors, and palpitations

prescription.name: Serum TSH, Free T3, and Free T4 Panel
prescription.instruction: Check every 4-6 weeks until thyroid levels stabilize

care: Avoid excessive heat and intense strenuous exertion while heart rate is elevated.
Promptly report sore throat or high fever to physician (risk of agranulocytosis).
Protect eyes with lubricating drops and sunglasses if Graves ophthalmopathy present.
diet: High-calorie diet with adequate protein during hypermetabolic weight loss phase.
Ensure calcium (1,200 mg/day) and Vitamin D3 to counteract bone turnover.
Avoid kelp, seaweed, and high-iodine supplements that fuel thyroid hormone synthesis.

Hypoglycemia.overview: A condition where blood glucose drops below normal levels (<70 mg/dL / 3.9 mmol/L), triggering shakiness, sweating, anxiety, confusion, and dizziness.

prescription.name: Fast-Acting Carbohydrates (Rule of 15)
prescription.instruction: Consume 15g fast-acting sugar immediately (1/2 cup fruit juice, 3-4 glucose tablets, or 3 tsp sugar in water)

prescription.name: Recheck Blood Glucose in 15 Minutes
prescription.instruction: If still <70 mg/dL, repeat 15g fast sugar; recheck until normalized

prescription.name: Complex Snack Following Resolution
prescription.instruction: Eat a snack containing complex carb and protein (peanut butter toast, crackers + cheese)

care: Always carry glucose tablets or hard candies with you at all times.
Wear a medical alert identification bracelet indicating hypoglycemia risk.
Review medication dosages with doctor if episodes happen frequently.
diet: Eat regular, evenly spaced meals; never skip meals or delay carbohydrate intake.
Pair complex carbohydrates with protein and healthy fats to stabilize absorption.
Avoid alcohol on an empty stomach as it severely blunts hepatic glucose release.

Osteoarthristis.overview: The most common form of arthritis, involving progressive breakdown of joint cartilage and underlying bone, resulting in joint pain, stiffness, and crepitus.

prescription.name: Paracetamol 650mg / Topical NSAID Gel (Diclofenac 1%)
prescription.instruction: First-line therapy; apply gel to affected joint 3-4 times daily

prescription.name: Glucosamine & Chondroitin Sulfate
prescription.instruction: Take daily nutritional formulation to support cartilage lubrication

prescription.name: Intra-articular Hyaluronic Acid / Corticosteroid
prescription.instruction: Clinician-administered injection for severe refractory joint pain

care: Participate in low-impact joint-friendly exercise (swimming, stationary cycling, water aerobics).
Maintain optimal body weight: losing 1 pound reduces 4 pounds of pressure on knee joints.
Apply heat packs for morning joint stiffness, and cold packs after activity.
diet: Incorporate anti-inflammatory Mediterranean foods (olive oil, wild salmon, walnuts).
Eat foods high in Vitamin C and bioflavonoids to support collagen synthesis.
Minimize refined sugars and fried foods that promote systemic inflammatory cytokines.

Arthritis.overview: Systemic inflammatory or autoimmune joint disease marked by symmetrical synovitis, joint swelling, morning stiffness lasting >30 minutes, and fatigue.

prescription.name: Disease-Modifying Antirheumatic Drugs (DMARDs - Methotrexate)
prescription.instruction: Specialist rheumatology regimen to halt joint erosive progression

prescription.name: Celecoxib 200mg / Naproxen 500mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet daily with food for symptomatic joint inflammation

prescription.name: Folic Acid 5mg (Weekly)
prescription.instruction: Take on non-methotrexate day to minimize medication side effects

care: Consult a rheumatologist early; early DMARD initiation prevents joint deformity.
Balance regular gentle physical therapy with adequate joint rest during flares.
Use assistive devices or ergonomic joint-sparing tools in daily tasks.
diet: Anti-inflammatory diet rich in omega-3 fatty acids (salmon, mackerel, chia seeds).
Incorporate turmeric (curcumin) and ginger for natural anti-inflammatory benefits.
Limit red meat, processed carbohydrates, and excess saturated fats.

Psoriasis.overview: A chronic immune-mediated skin condition that accelerates the life cycle of skin cells, leading to thick, red patches covered with silvery scales.

prescription.name: Topical Clobetasol / Betamethasone Dipropionate Cream
prescription.instruction: Apply sparingly to thick plaques twice daily for 2 weeks, then taper

prescription.name: Calcipotriol (Vitamin D3 Analogue) Ointment
prescription.instruction: Apply to plaques once daily morning to slow skin cell turnover

prescription.name: Coal Tar / Salicylic Acid Shampoo
prescription.instruction: Lather on scalp, leave for 5-10 minutes before rinsing, 2-3 times weekly

care: Keep skin well-moisturized with thick emollient ointments immediately after bathing.
Get brief, controlled natural sunlight exposure (10-15 minutes, avoiding sunburn).
Avoid skin injury, scratching, and cuts (Koebner phenomenon triggers new plaques).
diet: Anti-inflammatory Mediterranean dietary pattern rich in colorful vegetables.
Reduce alcohol and tobacco consumption, both of which trigger flare-ups.
Incorporate omega-3 fish oils to modulate inflammatory eicosanoids.

Impetigo.overview: A highly contagious superficial bacterial skin infection (Staphylococcus or Streptococcus), presenting with characteristic honey-colored crusted erosions.

prescription.name: Mupirocin 2% Topical Ointment
prescription.instruction: Wash area, soak off crusts gently with warm water, apply ointment 3 times daily

prescription.name: Cephalexin 500mg (Oral Antibiotic)
prescription.instruction: Take 1 capsule 4 times daily if lesions are widespread, under doctor prescription

prescription.name: Antiseptic Chlorhexidine Wash
prescription.instruction: Cleanse surrounding skin gently once daily

care: Keep infected sores loosely covered with clean gauze to prevent scratching and spread.
Wash hands thoroughly after touching affected skin.
Wash patient towels, clothing, and bedding in hot water daily and do not share.
diet: Eat a well-rounded diet with high-protein foods to support rapid dermal healing.
Stay well-hydrated with clean water and herbal teas.
Incorporate foods containing Vitamin C and Zinc to support cutaneous immunity.

Urinary tract infection.overview: A bacterial infection of the urinary bladder or urethra, characterized by dysuria (burning urination), urinary urgency, pelvic ache, and cloudy urine.

prescription.name: Nitrofurantoin 100mg / Fosfomycin 3g
prescription.instruction: Take twice daily with meals as directed by physician following urine culture

prescription.name: Phenazopyridine 200mg
prescription.instruction: Take 1 tablet after meals for acute urinary burning (turns urine orange-red)

prescription.name: Urinary Alkalinizer (Disodium Hydrogen Citrate)
prescription.instruction: Mix 2 teaspoons in glass of water twice daily to soothe burning sensation

care: Drink at least 2.5 - 3.0 liters of water daily to flush bacteria from urinary tract.
Urinate promptly when you feel the urge; do not hold urine in bladder.
Wipe from front to back after using the bathroom to avoid introducing bacteria.
diet: Drink 100% pure unsweetened cranberry juice or take D-mannose supplements.
Avoid coffee, alcohol, carbonated drinks, and spicy foods that irritate the bladder.
Eat probiotic foods like plain unsweetened yogurt to replenish urogenital flora.
